newsitem.title: FINLAND: TAMRO SEES 1997 PROFIT STEADY VS 1996.
newsitem.headline: TAMRO SEES 1997 PROFIT STEADY VS 1996.

text.p: Finnish pharmaceuticals wholesaler Oy Tamro Ab said on Friday it saw no major changes 1997 profits compared to the 1996 level.
"We do not expect any major changes from the 1996 profit," Tamro's CEO Matti Elovaara told a news conference with the release of its preliminary 1996 earnings.
Tamro's full-year 1996 profit after financial items was 224 million markka compared to 155 million in 1995.
Tamro did not give a dividend proposal for 1996 but said:

"Provided that Tamro's financial development continues on a sound basis, the objective of the board of directors is that the company will pay a dividend of about 50 percent of the earnings per share."
Tamro's 1996 EPS was 1.73 markka, up from 1.33 markka in 1995. The dividend for 1995 was 0.70 markka per share.

Elovaara said Tamro aimed to become the market leader in the distribution of pharmaceuticals and in the marketing of medical and laboratory products in the Nordic countries, the Baltic states and northwest Russia.
Tamro's sales grew some 70 percent in the Baltic republics and Russia last year.
"We expect brisk sales growth in the region for 1997 as well, but we do not see it (the growth rate) reaching last year's levels," Elovaara said.
"It will be several tens of percent, though," he added.
